desc:
A great and recent calamity has occurred here. Vast sections of the tunnel walls
have collapsed blocking the passageway. There appears to be no way through.
name: A Dark Tunnel

desc:
The tunnel is dark and disgusting. You feel nauseous from breathing the stale
and disgusting air. However the walls and room appear firm and trustworthy.
name: A Dark Tunnel

desc:
The tunnel is dark and disgusting. You feel nauseous from breathing the stale
and disgusting air. However the walls and room appear firm and trustworthy.
name: A Dark Tunnel

desc:
You have entered a dark tunnel. The air is stale and smells disgusting. The
walls of the tunnel are shattered and broken and you fear that the roof itself
might collapse upon you.
name: A Dark Tunnel

desc:
You have entered a dark tunnel. The air is stale and smells disgusting. The
walls of the tunnel are shattered and broken and you fear that the roof itself
might collapse upon you.
name: A Dark Tunnel

desc:
You are in a tunnel that seems old and unfinished. The walls are in places
smooth and in other places rough. It is as if a work long ago begun was
completed by other less skilled hands. The air here stinks and you feel
reluctant to proceed.
name: A Tunnel

desc:
This peculiar side passage seems to burrow indiscriminately through the thick
dirt itself. Only creatures of massive strength could attempt such a feat, but
the lack of any refinements indicates a lack for the finer points of
construction. The smell of filth and loam fills the air.
name: A Gutted Tunnel

desc:
Onwards, the tunnel continues, a gaping maw carved in the very ground of Arda.
Roots stick out from all directions, as well as the blind eyes of very large
earthworms. The thick rancid smell of troll pervades the tunnel, leaving no
doubts as to who carved this path.
name: A Gutted Tunnel

desc:
This tunnel is actually quite large for one beneath the ground. The thick dirt
and debris indicate you are not far from the surface, yet you feel closed in by
the dark, uneven surfaces.
name: A Gutted Tunnel

desc:
These tunnels must be near the surface, for the walls are of packed earth and a
few intrepid tree roots dangle from the ceiling. The floor of the passage is
bedrock, and the tunnel dives down to the south through a fissure in the rocks.
To the east, this tunnel continues.
name: Bend in the Passage

desc:
Water drips from a chamber overhead, dampening the mixture of packed earth and
stone that makes up the floor. Heavy footprints are clearly visible leading to
the east. Crude steps have been hewn to aid in clambering up to the chamber
above.
name: Damp Intersection

desc:
A rockfall dominates the eastern half of this chamber. Large slabs of rock and
copious amounts of dirt have fallen from the ceiling, leaving a pile of rubble
below and a cavernous expanse above. The rockfall appears to have broken through
into an existing passage below; two particularly large slabs of stone have
become wedged above this opening, creating an impromptu archway and keeping the
opening from becoming obstructed. In the western half of the chamber, away from
the rockfall, a number of crude beds of leaves and scattered bones indicate that
this chamber is used as a sleeping area for trolls.
name: Partially-collapsed Chamber

desc:
This chamber of packed earth has its walls strengthened by many tree roots.
Apparently this must be near the surface, but no hint of fresh air can be felt.
Water is leaking from the ceiling, and the droplets that hit the floor coalesce
into small rivulets that drain through the hole in the floor. There are some
crude steps cut into the wall to help one to climb out of here.
name: Upper Chamber

desc:
This crude but functional flight of stairs has been crafted in the simplest of
ways: a series of stone slabs of various shapes and sizes has been arranged to
secure footholds along a steeply-angled shaft. The top of the stairs leads to a
large opening, while the lower part veers off in an eastwardly direction. In
contrast to the turning and sloping nature of the stone steps, an almost
horizontal shaft cuts a path southwards through the rock and soil.
name: Crudely-built Staircase

desc:
With nothing supporting this tunnel except the occasional latticework of roots,
there is little to suggest that this is the handiwork of skilled craftsmen. The
walls are part dirt, part bare rock; the rock seems to have been tunneled
through with little care, and bears deep scars from the crude excavation
process. A deep and earthy smell hangs heavily in the air, partially masking a
faint undertone of something far more acrid.
name: A Crude, Earthy Tunnel

desc:
A crude shaft, the walls bearing scars from a hasty excavation process, allows
passage either further into the depths below, or up the slope to the west. The
bare stone floor is etched with deep grooves, presumably the result of large and
heavy objects being dragged or pushed from one place to another.
name: A Dark Shaft

desc:
The earthy tunnel walls give way to bare rock to the north and east. No attempts
appear to have been made to tunnel through the rock; the tunnel instead bends
here, following a path of least resistance through the softer soil. A crevice in
the rock to the north extends from the ceiling of the tunnel all the way to the
floor, widening and deepening as it descends; at the level of the floor it is
large enough to allow access as it continues straight down into the cave system.
name: A Crude, Earthy Tunnel

desc:
A tunnel of varied width snakes its way further through the soil and bedrock as
it continues from south to north. The crude craftsmanship suggested both by the
irregular sizing of the tunnel, and the chunks of broken rock and hacked-up
roots left in piles along the walls, indicates a hasty excavation. The southern
part of the tunnel narrows considerably as it reaches a natural grotto.
name: A Crude, Earthy Tunnel

desc:
A small, natural grotto lies nestled deep within the bedrock and loose soil. The
smooth, aged surface of the rock suggests that it is indeed a naturally
occurring cavern, and not the result of digging. This impression is underscored
by a contrasting, roughly-cut tunnel that has left a gaping hole through the
rock and soil to the north. Debris piles have been left at the junction of
tunnel and grotto, almost as if someone or something broke through the wall with
sheer force.
name: Natural Grotto

desc:
A slightly-slanted tunnel offers passage through the dark, smooth bedrock.
Though the smooth walls of the tunnel suggest a natural origin, someone has made
makeshift steps by hacking away at the floor to provide better footholds. There
is a large opening leading downwards, wide enough to cater to even the largest
of beasts.
name: Natural Passageway

desc:
Debris from a cave-in covers the ground in this partially-obscured passageway.
The tunnel tapers off into a seemingly impassable crawlspace to the east while
the western direction offers a far more conveniently-sized opening.
Partially-eaten remnants of humanoid corpses have been left near the rockfall.
name: A Caved-in Passageway

desc:
The walls of the tunnel here are jagged: the surrounding bedrock is broken and
cracked, leaving deep crevices and protruding edges. The passageway itself is
relatively level; the rock underfoot forms a somewhat concave surface as it
slopes up to form the surrounding walls. Droplets of water have beaded on the
smoother of the surrounding surfaces, and the air is damp and cool.
name: Natural Passageway

desc:
The western end of this tunnel has caved in, leaving a pile of dirt and broken
rocks. The rockfall appears to have originated in a cavern above and broken
through into this passageway; two particularly large slabs of stone have wedged,
leaning against each other, to form an impromptu archway while keeping the
access-way into the cave above clear from debris. As the tunnel continues to the
east, away from the rockfall, the surrounding stone becomes smooth, suggesting
that this tunnel was formed naturally by water running through the bedrock long
ago.
name: Partially-collapsed Passage

desc:
Deep furrows mar floor and walls alike throughout the shaft. Rocks of varying
shape and size are scattered along the passageway; some were clearly broken from
the deep gouges in the walls, while the comparatively lighter colours of others
suggest that they did not originate in this part of the tunnel. A faint, putrid
odour hangs in the air.
name: A Dark Shaft

desc:
Strong odours fill this large cavern. The walls, roughly-cut from the
surrounding stone, suggest that this cave is not a natural feature. Large piles
of refuse, consisting of a mix of debris, faeces, bones and half-rotted pieces
of flesh, have been deposited throughout. A smaller cave has been dug in the
bedrock to the north, while passageways to the south and east grant access to a
nearby network of tunnels.
name: A Refuse-littered Cavern

desc:
Excavation tools, both broken and functional, have been piled on the floor of
this cave. The curious presence of shackles and lengths of chain may indicate
that the cave is used as storage for living creatures as well as inanimate
objects; nothing, however, is currently chained here. A putrid smell hangs heavy
in the air towards the southern end of the cave.
name: Storage Cave

desc:
Walls of rock to the east and west press in close here, creating a vertical
shaft that drops straight down into the depths of the cave system. The walls
appear to be made from great shelves of stone, stacked unevenly upon each other
to form tall but shallow steps and recesses; the resulting ledges are too far
apart to be used ladder-like when ascending or descending, and are mostly too
shallow to be stood upon. One ledge, wider than the rest, is wide enough to
allow purchase; it is precarious, however, slick from condensation and the piles
of bat guano that cover every horizontal surface.
name: Precarious Ledge

desc:
Piles of refuse partially obstruct this passage. Those nearest to the centre of
the tunnel have been trampled down by passing feet; bones, skins, and faecal
matter have been spread from wall to wall, creating a slightly slippery layer
that covers the bedrock beneath. Closer to the walls the piles are less
disturbed; some are heaped nearly to the ceiling, their contents buried beneath
a moving layer of large, iridescent flies. The air here is thick with the odours
of putrefaction and faeces.
name: A Refuse-littered Tunnel

desc:
A wide but low space opens up here at the juncture of several tunnels. The rock
overhead is pitted, hinting at many aborted attempts to enlarge this cavern; the
rubble obstructing the passageways suggests that not all attempts were in vain.
Several distinct paths have been cleared through the piles of dirt and broken
rock, although several large boulders have not been moved from the centre of the
junction, the point at which all paths meet.
name: Subterranean Juncture

desc:
Broken rock fills this passage, creating unstable footing and making the ceiling
appear low. The cracks in the ceiling, paired with several badly-broken sheets
of stone on top of the rubble, suggest that there was a minor collapse here at
some point in the past. The original floor of the tunnel has been buried under
fallen rock, but enough space remains to allow passage from north to east.
name: Rubble-filled Tunnel

desc:
Huge chunks of broken rock fill this part of the tunnel, resulting in a low
ceiling and difficult passage. The rubble is stable; most of the rocks are large
or tightly-packed enough not to shift underfoot, although in spots narrow
crevices extend a significant distance downwards. The rubble is piled highest
along the walls, reaching almost all the way to the ceiling; it appears that the
rubble in the centre of the tunnel has been pushed aside, creating a slightly
more level, and spacious, path.
name: Rubble-filled Tunnel

desc:
Broken rocks are piled in the western part of this passageway, reaching nearly
to the ceiling and creating difficult obstacles over which to pass. A path has
been partially cleared through the centre of the rubble, the rocks pushed to
either side; the path extends into the tunnel to the west, which is similarly
obstructed. In the eastern part of this passage, however, the rubble has been
completely cleared away, revealing a spacious tunnel that slopes downwards.
name: Rubble-filled Tunnel

desc:
A wide burrow of hard-packed dirt runs from north to south. The walls to the
east and west widen considerably before the dirt gives way to solid rock; deep
gouges in the rock suggest that attempts were made to expand this tunnel in both
directions before being abandoned in favour of easier passage through the soil.
The air is cool and damp in this part of the tunnel; it has a strong earthy
scent that carries a hint of mould and decay.
name: Earthy Burrow

desc:
A tunnel winds through the hard-packed dirt here, curving from west to north.
The walls and the ceiling of the tunnel are furrowed, creating ridges that
appear to spiral down the passage. Some of the deeper furrows have exposed an
underlying layer of rock; in places this rock has scratches and gouges,
presumably left over from the excavation process.
name: Earthy Burrow

desc:
Walls of rock to the east and west press in close, creating a natural fissure
that starts here and extends upwards. The bottom of the fissure is covered with
gravel and larger rocks that have broken from the walls; some of the gravel is a
lighter colour than the surrounding rock, suggesting that it has fallen from
much higher up. The western wall is smooth and almost completely vertical, while
the eastern wall is staggered, the stone alternately angled inwards to form
recesses and outwards to form shallow ledges. One of these recesses gives way to
an earthy tunnel that cuts under the rock ledge above; it is wide and tall, and
does not appear to have been formed naturally.
name: Narrow Walls

desc:
The slope in this part of the shaft becomes steep as its descent continues to
the south. The rock that forms the floor of the shaft has been dug out crudely,
creating a tunnel floor that is neither level nor smooth; passage through the
shaft here is made easier by this irregular footing, as the raised chunks of
rock and deep gouges serve as footholds on the steep slope. The air is cool and
slightly damp, with moisture beading on the furrowed rock walls.
name: A Dark Shaft

desc:
The solid, coarse-grained granite has been excavated to create a sort of
crossroads deep underground. The excavation must have required great effort; the
very core of the hard, unforgiving bedrock has given way in the face of brute
strength and hard-headed will. White marks are faintly visible on the dark stone
surfaces, left over from the scraping of metal against stone. Tunnels diverge in
five directions, and the rugged walls quickly fade from sight around corners and
down slopes.
name: Hollowed-out Core

desc:
This tunnel runs horizontally as it cuts through the rock from north to south.
The stone underfoot is rough but level, and a layer of dirt has accumulated on
the ground near the tunnel walls. A series of small cracks in the walls seems to
be the source of the dirt; it is being squeezed through the cracks slowly by the
pressure from above, and is piling up along the edges of the tunnel. The
resulting smooth transition from walls to ground gives this narrow passage a
slightly rounded appearance.
name: Narrow Drift

desc:
A tunnel leads here from the west, through the solid grey granite bedrock. The
tunnel tapers to nothing; perhaps the effort required to dig through the hard
rock became too great, and the attempt was abandoned. The walls are laced with
cracks and the gouges from pick axes and other instruments used in the digging;
clearly, not even trolls could dig through this rock without tools.
name: Dead-end Tunnel

desc:
Here, the digging activities of the trolls have run into a large, natural
cavern. Tunnel openings in the northeast corner of the cave show where the
trolls burst through the wall as they were burrowing; large, broken stones are
piled near the openings, having been pushed aside but not removed. The ceiling
is high, and the cavern floor is littered with huge, craggy boulders of various
sizes.
name: Expansive, Bouldered Cavern

desc:
The tunnel slopes sharply here, coming from the north and leading upwards; it
forms a wide, steep ramp. The surface underfoot is littered with small, sharp
chunks of rock that roll and slide underfoot, hindering passage up the slope.
Near the top of the ramp these rocks become more numerous and much larger,
forming a layer of rubble that shifts when walked upon. The ceiling overhead
slopes at less of an angle than the floor, creating a more restricted tunnel
near the top of the ramp, and a more spacious one at the bottom.
name: Steep Ramp

desc:
This oddly-coloured dirt tunnel leads further north, while a spacious cavern
opens to the south. The dirt that composes the surrounding walls and ceiling is
a deep reddish-brown colour; small trickles of water running down the walls seem
to pick up the reddish tones, creating rivulets with the appearance of blood.
The air here is cool and still, and a faint metallic smell can be detected
beneath the heavy earthy odour that fills the tunnel.
name: Tunnel of Blood-red Dirt

desc:
A rock wall curves around here from east to south, forming the northwestern
corner of this huge cavern. The ceiling above is cracked, pitted, and uneven; it
is possible that some of the many sharp-angled boulders strewn across the floor
here have fallen from above. The presence of truncated columns in various places
support this possibility; they appear to have been at one time growing
stalagmites, but are now broken, smashed by the same huge rocks that now demand
circuitous pathways when traversing the cavern.
name: Expansive, Bouldered Cavern

desc:
The southern wall in this part of the cavern appears to have caved in at some
point in the past; a large rockfall has spread outwards towards the middle of
the cave, creating an uneven slope that extends from the ceiling down to the
floor. A significant amount of dirt is mixed in with the rubble, and has been
spread across the cave floor; many large footprints can be seen in the dirt,
forming criss-crossing paths that extend in every direction.
name: Expansive, Bouldered Cavern

desc:
An enormous cavern opens up here and extends to the north and east. Giant
boulders and cracked slabs of stone litter the cave floor; some of these are
smooth, but most are badly pitted and eroded. Small spider webs fill the
pockmarks in some of the stones, and larger webs are stretched between the
crevices created where several rocks have been stacked together. Some of these
stacks of stones are irregular and suggestive of rockfall rather than purposeful
construction.
name: Expansive, Bouldered Cavern

desc:
The basin is narrow here, barely twelve feet from wall to wall in the widest
part. If it did not continue to the north, this would be little more than a
water-filled hole. The walls look black beneath the water, but on closer
examination appear to be made from a grey, rough-grained granite. The bottom is
uneven, and several loose rocks rest upon it; perhaps they have fallen from
above.
name: Bottom of a Basin

desc:
The water in this subterranean basin is cloudy with dirt and unidentifiable
particles of organic matter. A layer of sediment is visible on the bottom of the
basin; when the water is disturbed, the sediment rises to cloud the water and
reduce visibility. The rock overhead is grey and dark; it forms a smooth
expanse, unbroken by crevices or pockets that could trap air. The basin widens
slightly towards the north, and narrows to the south.
name: Underground Basin

desc:
An uneven, rugged tunnel has been cut through the hard, grey, granite bedrock.
Large chunks of rock protrude from the ground, pebbles litter the slope, and
loose rocks lie where their downhill roll was stopped by the aforementioned
obstacles. Further down the tunnel, the bottom of the passageway is visible.
name: Sloping Tunnel

desc:
This tunnel has been dug through the coarse-grained granite bedrock, and
tremendous effort and determination must have been required to tunnel through
such dense, hard stone. The cavern continues to the west and east. To the east
it slopes down steeply. The rock surface of the slope is covered with furrows
and gouges; it looks as if the rocks broken loose during the digging were simply
dumped into the tunnel and down the slope.
name: Sloping Tunnel

desc:
This deep, narrow passage has filled with water. A sediment layer is visible on
the bottom of the basin, and is stirred up when the water is disturbed. The
walls and bottom are of solid rock, and the sharp edges of protruding stones
clearly show that this is a body of still water, because flowing water would
have smoothed the edges over time. The pool is not deep here, and the
reflections from the surface above are clearly visible.
name: Bottom of a Basin

desc:
The passageway here, a tunnel through bedrock of coarse grey granite, has
collapsed with devastating results. The floor disappears into a jagged hole with
the bottom barely visible below. On the far side of the hole the continuing
tunnel is forever sealed by enormous masses of fallen rubble. The tunnel
continues to the east: following it in that direction may be safer than
attempting to climb down into the hole.
name: Dangerous Cave-in

desc:
This tunnel has been dug out of the surrounding rich, reddish-brown soil. The
soil is loose, and crumbles away from the walls and ceiling easily; various
furrows and pits in the surrounding surfaces are evidence of either natural
erosion or purposeful digging. The air here is cool and damp, with the
occasional draft coming from the east.
name: Tunnel of Blood-red Dirt

desc:
This soft-walled tunnel, comprised of a curious reddish-brown soil, comes to a
dead end here. The soil underfoot at the end of the tunnel is very densely
packed; above, a large, irregularly-shaped hole can be seen. The air stirs at
irregular intervals as drafts blow down from the hole. However, as the hole is
too high to reach, the only passable exit is to the west.
name: Tunnel of Blood-red Dirt

desc:
A ravine opens up towards the south. The hollow in the northern wall of the
ravine provides a stony roof above, offering some protection from the elements.
This grotto could possibly mark the beginning of a deeper cave, as a huge bear
fur hung against the inner wall seems to cover an entrance deeper into the
underground.
name: Rocky Shelter

desc:
While this was in all likelihood a natural cavern in the past, it has been
expanded with crude tools to form a wide, high-ceilinged corridor. On the roof
above, broken remnants of stalactites cling to the rock. Anything reaching down
below ten feet has been hewn off, leaving jagged, shattered remains. On the
lightly grey limestone floor, any stalagmites rising up to meet the opposing
stalactites have been removed with brute force. The now widened corridor leads
deeper into a cavern to the west, while a huge bear fur has been hung on the
southern wall to cover what looks like a narrowing tunnel.
name: Limestone Corridor

desc:
These caves may well be natural in origin but have been converted into a rustic
living area by whomever that now occupy them. Rocks or boulders one would expect
in a cave have been cleared out, and the ground is worn smooth by the regular
passage of its inhabitants. Towards the west, the cave leads through a narrow
opening from which scents of meat and blood come drifting on the slowly
circulating air.
name: Wide Diverging Tunnel

desc:
Four tunnels lead off in different directions from this subterranean juncture.
The cavern is lofty, the ceiling no less than ten feet high at its lowest point.
A vague scent of wood smoke fills the air, hinting at a recent fire in one of
the nearby caves.
name: The Juncture

desc:
This wide tunnel takes a rough, uneven path through the surrounding rock, moving
through this area in a south-to-west bend. A small spring seeps up from the
cavern floor at the eastern wall, gathering in a small pool to provide fresh
water. The dust on the ground is mostly cleared away in a path from the pool and
towards the south; although more because of regular traffic than any obvious
intent to keep the area neat and clean. The tunnel to the west seem a lot less
disturbed.
name: Wide Tunnel by a Spring

desc:
This narrow cave has been converted into a crude larder. The walls are speckled
with spots of dried blood, and on the dusty floor dark, drying stains attract
flies and other insects. Simple iron hooks have been set into the walls, ready
for whatever meats may be hung from them.
name: Stone Giant's Larder

desc:
A low, narrow opening to the west seem to be the only entrance to this dwelling.
The interior is stark, the walls harsh bare stone and the floor rough and
uneven. Three tall piles of grass, leaves and animal furs could be passed off as
sleeping places, and the scorched stones in the centre of the chamber suggest
that at times a fire is built here.
name: Stark Dwelling

desc:
A very large set of stairs has been hewn out of the hard rock, leading further
down into deep caverns. The cavern floor has been cleared of irregularities and
any sharp or protruding stone has been removed from the walls. With a little
decoration and lighting, this cave could almost pass as a hallway.
name: Top of Stone Stairs

desc:
The tunnel enters this wide, spacious grotto from the east. To the south and
west, hard solid walls of rock block any passage, but towards the north the cave
opens up and the far wall is barely discernible. Travel northwards is
interrupted by a jagged crevice, and the only obvious way onwards in that
direction is to climb down into the crevice and find a way from there.
name: Shelf above a Crevice

desc:
This crevice is narrow, with steep and jagged walls and sharp rocks everywhere.
At the very southwestern end of the crevice, a rock shelf is visible. This looks
to be the only reasonable place to climb out of here. If one were inclined to
stay in the crevice, it appears to continue eastwards.
name: Underground Crevice

desc:
Huge steps have been hewn out of the solid rock to the west, where a slight
slope ascends and provides easier passage to the levels above. Each step is so
high that a hobbit would need to use his hands to climb to the next, and so wide
that said hobbit could place his bed on it. The cavern floor looks well trodden,
free of loose rocks and remarkably smooth.
name: Foot of Stone Stairs

desc:
The cavern system comes to a dead end here, and this small cave has been
converted to a crude abode. Judging from the size of the long, wooden bunks
against the back wall, the inhabitants are of impressive dimensions. The walls
are rough but seem to have been smoothened to some extent, the worst of the
sharp edges chopped away.
name: Crude Abode

desc:
This deep cleft is barely passable. The broken, jagged rocks of the crevice's
walls makes travel to the east and west very difficult. Climbing out of the deep
fissure is completely out of the question, the sides being much too steep, the
rock cracked and broken; and most likely prone to falling apart if any weight is
put upon it. The ground is littered with rubble fallen from the walls.
name: Deep in an Underground Crevice

desc:
Here at the eastern end of this crevice, deep beneath the surface, little hope
is given to a weary adventurer. The bottom of this crevice is a bleak place, the
ground littered with broken rocks and fallen rubble. The sides of the deep
fissure appear impossible to climb and the only viable direction of travel is to
follow the course of the crevice towards the west.
name: Eastern End of an Underground Crevice

desc:
Here, the vast cavern that extends west of here ends in a small retreat. Lots of
rubble lies strewn across the cavern floor, fallen from the unstable roof above.
Most of the cavern walls and gravel consists of hard, grey stone prone to
breaking apart into smaller shards with sharp, jagged edges.
name: Rubble-strewn Cavern

desc:
The size of this wide, vast cavern would put the throne room in many a castle to
shame. The walls stand far enough apart to be shrouded in inky gloom. A great
aggregation of rocky formations on the floor level makes the area hard to
navigate. The floor itself is full of cracks, some of which are wide enough to
step into if one were careless.
name: Vast Natural Cavern

desc:
A cave-in has created an enormous mass of crushed boulders along a wall in this
colossal cavern. Any pathway in that direction has been lost forever. The
remainder of the cave can still be described as pasture-sized. The rock is of a
dark grey variety, and the rugged formations of the walls, floor and ceiling
leaves no doubt that this cave is a work of nature.
name: Vast Natural Cavern

desc:
Faint sounds of dripping water can be heard echoing from some dark corner of
this gigantic grotto. A wide variety of rocks make up the walls and floor, much
of it granite but also volcanic rock types. Pillars of basalt stand tall in the
stale air, remnants of chutes of volcanic magma that solidified in ages long
gone. There is also thin veins of pitch black obsidian embedded in the rock bed,
the slivers of glass-like rock glitter alluringly.
name: Deep in a Vast Cavern

desc:
A vast, natural cavern has formed here, deep down underground. The ground is
very uneven, with cliff-like formations several yards high that rise from the
floor throughout the cave. Much of the rock seem rich in ore, and there are
veins of a dark, rusty red colour and some of brighter yellow shades.
name: Deep in a Vast Cavern

desc:
This smaller tunnel connects two huge, open caverns to the east and west, while
to the north and south the walls of rough rock stand much closer together. The
ground falls away in a steep treacherous fall to the east. A heedless traveller
could walk right off the edge and crash down into the dark depths of this
subterranean world.
name: Edge of a Steep Cliff

desc:
This cave is shaped like a terrace with wide, stair-like ledges to the east and
west. Towards the west a cliff wall looms, so smooth it looks almost polished.
Eastwards, the cavern floor falls away again in another steep decline. A narrow
ledge leads out above the eastern chasm, following the southern cave wall in a
sharp bend, only to quickly disappear from sight.
name: Base of a Steep Cliff

desc:
This narrow, unsteady ledge clings to the rock face, painstakingly winding its
way southwards. To the west the ledge enters a cave, and footing is likely to be
more stable. The ledge itself is is littered with earth and pebbles. In places
there are gaps that must be stepped over, which further speak of the dangers of
loitering here.
name: Precarious Ledge

desc:
In places, this uneven ledge slopes downwards out from the rock face, and small
rocks and pebbles crunch underfoot: further heightening the risk of a fall. A
step in any direction seems hazardous and potentially fatal. At places the ledge
widens enough for easy passage, yet in other it is narrow enough that brushing
against the cave wall is inevitable.
name: Precarious Ledge

desc:
With a sharp twist, this tunnel bends toward the south and the east. The walls
are smooth and rounded, made of earth rather than hard rock. It is hard to say
if this is part of natural cave system or if this tunnel has been dug out.
Towards the east the tunnel open up into a wide space while it continues in a
slight downward slope to the south. The air is foul here, a stench of rot and
decay ever present as if something died and was left unburied.
name: Twisting Earth Tunnel

desc:
Droves of loose earth has fallen to the floor of this tunnel, making the footing
soft but taxing. The tunnel slopes down steeply toward the east to disappear
deeper into the ground. The tunnel seem much too rounded to be a creation of
nature, although there are no obvious sign of it being intentionally designed.
name: Earth Tunnel at the Top of a Slope

desc:
This serpentine, sloping earth tunnel winds its way down through layers of
densely packed earth. The tunnel seem to level out not far below this point,
although if that means that it is any closer to anything of relevance is
indeterminable. A long, wide groove runs along the centre of the tunnel, as if
something heavy was dragged along the floor recently.
name: Sloping Earth Tunnel

desc:
A deep furrow, almost a yard wide and half as deep, has been ploughed along this
tunnel. Something very heavy may have been either dragged or rolled through
here, going up the slope or coming down it. The walls hard-packed earth walls
are interspersed with small grey rocks of varying shapes.
name: Bottom of an Earth Tunnel

desc:
A large boulder blocks most of the underground ravine here, firmly embedded in
the mix of hard earth and gravel underfoot. Passage through the area requires
squeezing oneself between the boulder and the rugged walls of the ravine. Many
smaller rocks lie scattered across the ground, hinting at a roof above that is
far from stable.
name: Underground Ravine

desc:
The great ravine through the deep subterranean bedrock comes to its end here,
the sides simply coming together to meet at a solid wall of rock. Where the
ravine is a bit wider, there is an area where the northern wall is considerably
less steep than elsewhere. A tunnel opening lies there, the opening a black hole
against the surrounding stone.
name: Underground Ravine by an Incline

desc:
A narrow cavern to the north leads out onto this open area. The tunnel ends at
the very brink of an underground ravine at least twenty feet across. The slope
down to the ravine's floor is steep, but rugged and uneven and should be easy
enough to traverse. A cold draft can be felt from below, slightly rustling some
old, dead cobwebs that cling to the limestone walls.
name: Brink above a Ravine

desc:
This tunnel is filled with rubble and broken rocks, making the ceiling appear
low. Most of the rocks are large enough not to shift underfoot, although some
are unstable; passage over and through the rubble is made more difficult by the
latter, as sudden shifts can reveal surprisingly deep crevices in the otherwise
tightly-packed debris. The rubble has been cleared from the very southern part
of this tunnel, revealing a large and relatively level passageway; for whatever
reason, the rest of the tunnel has not been cleared in a similar fashion.
name: Rubble-filled Tunnel

desc:
This passage is near the surface, judging by the few tree roots that are
visible. Somewhere above lie the dark Trollshaws. The walls are made of packed
earth, hardened by the passage of time. However, any pleasant earthy smell is
overwhelmed by the foetid odour of trolls.
name: Twisted Passageway
